messages:
Priya K.: heads-up — seeing a backlog of GPU pods in us-west2-g; ~18 nodes each with 1 GPU free but scheduler keeps leaving pods pending. rebalancer didn't touch them overnight :confused:
Alex M.: oh interesting, is this the tiny-slot workload? any affinity/taint changes in the last 12h?
Priya K.: not that I saw. we rolled a security patch on the node-pool yesterday (labels applied) but no taints. kube events show '0/40 nodes had available gpu' for some pods even though nodes show allocable GPU.
Marco R.: can you paste the pod spec? sometimes gpu-request is 0.75 and we do fractional packing -> scheduler thinks it can't fit because of binpack scoring.
Priya K.: snippet: `resources: requests: nvidia.com/gpu: 1` pods are requesting 1.0. here's `kubectl get nodes -o=custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,GPU:.status.allocatable.nvidia\.com/gpu,alloc:.status.capacity.nvidia\.com/gpu` -> shows 1 free on many nodes.
Jen L.: rebalancer-bot might be in cooldown due to the drain phase yesterday. I saw a log about 'late-bind suppression'.
rebalancer-bot: Rebalance run skipped. cooldown_until=1744450500 reason="ongoing maintenance/drain windows"
Alex M.: that explains it. cooldown prevented gentle move. but why are scheduler predicates failing? any topology/zone affinity?
Priya K.: pods have `nodeSelector: gpu-type: a100-80gb` and nodes match. network tests to infra LB in the same AZ look fine. also saw `FailedScheduling` with `MatchNodeSelector` false in some events (odd).
Marco R.: could be label race: nodes got relabeled `gpu-type` after kubelet restart; scheduler cache and apiserver lag produced transient mismatch. then pods got stuck in pending and rebalancer cooldown prevented eviction-based fix.
Jen L.: cost note — these stranded single-gpu holes are causing burst autoscaler to spin up more nodes in other pools, increasing spot/commit spend. we saw ~12% GPU overprovision last 6h.
Alex M.: short-term: can we force a one-off rebalance run ignoring cooldown? or patch rebalancer to allow small-shelf fixes?
Priya K.: I'm +1 to a one-off. patch command: `curl -XPOST https://ops-api/rebalancer/run?force=true&reason=us-west2-g-shelf-skew`
oncall-bot: /run-rebalance accepted, queued job 4829, ETA ~2m
rebalancer-bot: forced run started. will only evict non-critical pods and prefer same-az moves. dry-run=false
Priya K.: rebalancer logs: `evicting 14 pods across 9 nodes, preferred_targets=local_rack`
Marco R.: nice. keep an eye for eviction storms — we should limit parallel evictions to 2 per-rack. also let's add a health-check to catch label churn: if node label updates >3 in 10m, pause rolling updates.
Jen L.: created an issue: https://github.com/redwood/infra/issues/3212 "preventing rebalancer cooldown holes + label-race mitigations". assigning Alex and Marco.
Alex M.: follow-ups: 1) add a preflight check to rebalancer to reconcile node labels with scheduler cache before deciding cooldown, 2) change default cooldown window from 3h -> 30m for maintenance-tagged drains, 3) add cost alert for >8% GPU overprovision per-region.
Priya K.: post-run status: pending queue dropped from 120 -> 6 in 10m, nodes with single free GPU reduced to 2. Keeping monitoring on the autoscaler.
oncall-bot: alert cleared: `us-west2-g gpu_pending_queue` at 1744450455
Priya K.: thanks all. will follow up in the GH issue with logs and a small K8s repro. :pray:
